text: Lilja and colleagues (153) conducted the most comprehensive human study to date on the topic in resistance-trained, young, healthy individuals. As opposed to previous work in young subjects (142), the study administered a higher dosage (1,200 mg/day vs. 400 mg/day of ibuprofen), and training was carried out over a longer study period (8 weeks vs. 6 weeks), thereby providing better insights into effects on muscular adaptations. Contrary to other findings, results showed that quadriceps growth in the NSAID group was blunted to approximately half that of the group receiving a placebo (3.7% vs. 7 .5%, respectively).
